findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: In the new `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` matcher the grant shortcut is extracted with `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 session type + 2 token type + 2 grant type), so the grant shortcut lives at indices 4..6, not 3..5. Additionally the check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false exactly when the grant matches. The combined effect is that the matcher accepts tokens with any grant type except (incorrectly offset) the expected one, so all the converted assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) do not actually verify the encoded grant and may pass/fail for the wrong reason. Should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` (with a length check on items[0]).

findings.title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again; `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null rawTokenId will silently pass and produce a token ID ending in "...:null" when encoded. Should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() on public SPI interface breaks existing custom grant implementations
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` lives in server-spi-private and is implemented by third-party extensions. Adding `String getShortcut();` without a default implementation makes all existing custom grant-type factories fail to compile/load (AbstractMethodError at runtime for pre-compiled providers). Consider providing a default implementation (e.g. derived/unknown shortcut) or documenting the breaking change in upgrade notes.

findings.title: Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor is a breaking SPI change
findings.body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted from this server-spi-private class. Any extension (or downstream code) that subclasses/copies the grant context will no longer compile or will fail at runtime. If removal is intended it should be noted as a breaking change; otherwise keep the constructor (copying the new `grantType` field as well).

findings.title: Possible NPE when client session has no user session
findings.body: `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` is dereferenced without a null check. `initToken` in TokenManager already receives a `UserSessionModel` parameter and some flows (e.g. token exchange with transient/detached sessions, or contexts built from a client session only) can have a null user session on the client session, which would throw an NPE while issuing a token. Either pass the user session explicitly into the encoder or guard for null and fall back to SessionType.UNKNOWN/TRANSIENT.

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut validation can be bypassed by lazy map refresh
findings.body: The size-comparison check for duplicate grant shortcuts only runs in `postInit`. `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` later insert entries lazily without re-validating, so a newly deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one will silently overwrite the shortcut→grant mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Consider validating on insert (e.g. `putIfAbsent` and logging/erroring on conflict).
